stories.title: Mumbai terror attack survivor 'Baby Moshe' pursues rabbinical studies in New York

article_sentences: Mumbai: Moshe Holtzberg, the Israeli boy popularly known as 'Baby Moshe' who survived the 2008 Nariman House terror attack that claimed his parents' lives, is pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and aspires to become a rabbi like his father.

Rabbi Israel Kozlovsky, who is in charge of Nariman House, one of the places targeted by Pakistani Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists during the November 26, 2008 attacks, said he met Moshe two weeks ago at a rabbinical conference in New York.

"The conference was attended by 4,000 to 5,000 rabbis from across the world, and Moshe was also present," Kozlovsky said, showing a photograph on his mobile phone of Moshe posing in traditional attire alongside other rabbis.
A rabbi is a spiritual leader, religious teacher and legal scholar.
In the photograph, the once two-year-old 'Baby Moshe', whose footage of sobbing inconsolably after the attack drew global attention and moved millions, appears as a 20-year-old man.
"He is currently pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and wants to become a rabbi.
Hopefully, he will return to India.
That is our hope," Kozlovsky told PTI.
Moshe's parents, Rabbi Gavriel Holtzberg and mother Rivka Holtzberg, were killed when terrorists stormed the Chabad House, a centre that served the Jewish community here.
Moshe's nanny, Sandra Samuel, rescued him from the building and fled.
He later moved to Israel to stay with his grandparents.
He last visited Nariman House in 2018 alongside Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

stories.title: 30 missing terrorists from Reasi exfiltrated to Pak for arms training, disturb peace in India: DGP
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 25: Thirty terrorists hailing from Reasi district, who had gone missing between 1991 and 2003, have exfiltrated to Pakistan and are working for a terror outfit, supplying arms, ammunition and money to revive terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir, Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat said on Wednesday. The police chief said Mahore Police Station received information through reliable sources that 30 terrorists hailing from Mahore and Chassana, missing since 1991 to 2003, had crossed over to Pakistan for weapons training for waging war against India. "These persons are now working for HM (Hizbul Mujahideen) in Pakistan and are supplying arms and ammunition, money, to promote terrorism in J&K, besides instigating and radicalising the youth for taking part in terror activities in the area," the DGP said on X. The 30 terrorists operating from Pakistan have been identified as Mohd Qayoom of Shadole, Mohd Sabdar of Shajroo, Ghulam Mohd and Ghulam Qadir, both sons of Samdoo and residents of Khour, Mushtaq Ahmad of Khour and Khushal Hussain, a resident of Dada. The list further names Abdul Majeed, Mohd Rafiq, alias Shabir, Shabir Ahmad and Manzoor Ahmad, all residents of Karmkatha, Makhna and Alaf Din, both residents of Shajroo, Abdul Majeed of Lar, Ghulam Mohd, alias Gamma, of Shajroo, and Mushtaq Ahmad of Sildhar. Others identified are Mohd Yousuf Khakmat, alias Bilal (callsign), of Shadool, Mohd Iqbal and Mohd Ashraf, both residents of Chakrass, Ghulam Mohd of Ladh, Abdul Hamid Najar, alias Mahamdoo, of Shibrass, Jamal Din of Sildhar, and Talib Hussain of Chiklass. The remaining names are Mohd Rafiq, Gami Gujjar, both residents of Larh, Mohd Rafiq of Tulli, Mohd Qasim of Kunderdhan, Abdul Hamid of Balmatkote, Shabir Ahmad of Bagodass, Mohd Rafiq of Kunderdhan, and Mohd Ali of Hassote. In 2024, Mahore police filed an FIR under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Explosive and Im­provised Materials Control provisions and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against these alleged terrorists. During the investigation, police recorded statements of witnesses and identified five alleged terrorists who also exfiltrated to Pakistan for arms and ammunition training and were actively involved in attempts to revive terrorist activities in the area from across the border by selling their lands to finance terrorism, the DGP said. They have been identified as Mohd Qayoom, alias Abdul Qayoom, of Shadole in Mahore tehsil, Bashir Ahmad, alias Masoom, of Bidder, Shokat Ali of Hunder in Arnas tehsil, Manzoor Ahmad, alias Manzoor Hussain, of Khanti in Thuroo tehsil, and Imtyaz Ahmad of Thuroo. Police also seized over 27 kanals of land belonging to these five Reasi terrorists.

stories.headline: Indian markets defy global meltdown
stories.title: Indian markets defy global meltdown
stories.summary: While concerns over AI capital expenditure, chipmakers’ earnings and lofty valuations have triggered a global market sell-off, Indian equities remain relatively insulated, given their limited exposure to these risks. Unlike the US, where a handful of AI-linked stocks have dominated market performance, India’s rally has been underpinned by broader earnings growth and domestic liquidity.As worries mount over the sustainability of the AI-driven rally in developed markets, investors are increasingly reallocating capital to markets with stronger fundamental visibility. This has helped Indian benchmark indices, the Sensex and the Nifty, gain over 10 percent in the last six weeks, making India one of the standout markets amid the global turbulence. On Wednesday, the BSE Sensex and the Nifty gained around 2 percent each.In contrast, other Asian markets are on the decline. Asian technology stocks slid on Wednesday, with Japanese semiconductor stocks bearing the brunt of the sell-off, as fresh concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade spilled over from Wall Street and weighed on investor sentiment. South Korea’s Kospi slumped over 6 percent, while Japan’s Nikkei fell nearly 3 percent.“None of these issues should really affect India except from a sentiment perspective obliquely (AI versus non-AI markets). For India, earnings and oil prices will matter more,” says Sanjeev Prasad, managing director and co-head, Kotak Institutional Equities. He expects increased volatility in the near term for Indian markets, given their exposure to global investment sentiment.Also Read: Ashishkumar Chauhan: The man who transformed the marketsPrasad also notes that the Indian markets would have to contend with a sharper fall in other developed markets and emerging markets in the past month, a sharp deterioration in global risk sentiment and/or a possible resurgence of the ‘AI trade’.“We expect Indian market returns to be largely driven by crude prices in the near term and earnings in the medium term. The sharp run-up in the market and stocks across ‘consumption’ sectors in the past week would suggest that the market is already factoring in lower crude oil prices and higher margins in FY28,” Prasad elaborates.Prasad is not alone in his optimism. In November, many foreign brokerages renewed their bullish stance on India, betting on the domestic market as an alternative to AI trades. The likes of Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, CLSA, Jefferies, Citi and HSBC have turned more constructive on Indian equities, upgrading their outlook as they see India as both a key beneficiary and diversifier in the AI era—attractive valuations and a favourable earnings growth outlook have further strengthened the investment case.Indian stocks: The new-found loveAnalysts at Goldman Sachs expect the Nifty to reach 28,500 by end-2027, driven by 15 percent earnings growth. “India’s growth has remained resilient despite US tariffs, equity portfolio outflows and the latest Middle East conflict-driven energy shock. Timely fiscal support, earlier monetary easing, and strong credit growth cushioned activity,” they say.However, as financial conditions tighten and the effects of tax cuts fade, Goldman Sachs expects real gross domestic product (GDP) growth to moderate but remain strong at 7.2 percent year-on-year in 2027, supported by a nascent recovery in the private capex cycle. The analysts are also optimistic that the worst is likely over for the rupee, which is supported by robust services exports, remittances, and improved capital flows.For Ridham Desai and Nayant Parekh, equity strategists at Morgan Stanley, Indian stocks appear to be at an inflection point and could do significantly better next year. “It is rare that growth is accelerating, valuations are relatively inexpensive and sentiment is negative. In our view, this could support higher stock prices in the coming months,” say Desai and Parekh.As markets adopted a risk-off stance in October amid uncertainty surrounding the outcome of the US midterm elections, India stood out as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) returned, even as investors pared their exposure to global equities.Also Read: Has the tide really turned for Indian markets?In early November, CLSA was among the first foreign brokerages to upgrade India to ‘overweight’, anticipating a gradual revival in investor appetite for Indian stocks. “India’s anti-AI trade label is turning from a liability into an asset,” said Alexander Redman, chief equity strategist, CLSA.Jefferies has also increased India's weighting in its Asia-Pacific ex-Japan relative-return portfolio to 15 percent, from 13.3 percent. “Financial markets continue to act like the AI capex cycle has peaked, in spite of a lack of any compelling evidence as yet of any such development on the ground. Greed and fear will continue to assume for now that the market signal is the correct one where the only issue is whether this is the peak of the cycle or a mid-cycle correction,” Christopher Wood, global head of equity strategy, Jefferies, wrote in his latest note on November 19.Desai and Parekh similarly argue that any cooling in the AI capex theme could shift investor focus to India’s stronger earnings and structural growth story. According to Desai and Parekh, India offers durable, diversified and decoupled growth—characteristics that will likely create upside potential for Indian stocks if the AI capex story wanes and/or geopolitics settle down. In any case, India's earnings growth cycle is gaining traction. They explain that this is important because a principal catalyst for India to outperform in 2027 is how the market gauges the earnings growth gap between India and the world.“High-frequency indicators look solid, underscoring an up-cycle from improving investments, monetary policy support, an undervalued currency, lack of fiscal headwinds, and robust consumer sentiment,” Desai and Parekh add.Also Read: Nifty 50 pay hikes trail inflationFIIs flock to IndiaForeign investors have poured nearly $16 billion into Indian equities since October 16, indicating a dramatic shift in sentiment after an extended period of selling. The immediate catalyst is largely external, says Prateek Ancha, chief economist, Axis Capital.“An October correction in crowded AI trades, a sharp political setback for Republicans in the November elections, and the leadership upheaval at Nvidia. Together, these developments have raised the hurdle rate for financing the next generation of US data centres. India offers diversification: A domestic-demand-led earnings base and lower direct exposure to the AI theme,” adds Ancha.FIIs sold $2.2 billion worth of Indian equities in October, lower than the outflows recorded in the previous month. In contrast, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) invested $6.3 billion, extending their strong buying momentum for the 39th consecutive month.Meanwhile, an analysis by Axis Capital shows that, as foreign equity flows have turned positive since mid-October, India’s outperformance relative to emerging-market peers has lifted its benchmark weight by 4 percentage points.“Equity valuations appear inexpensive, cycle-adjusted, relative to history,” say Desai and Parekh. They feel that the earnings cycle has resumed its upward journey, helped by an emerging private capex cycle, the releveraging of corporate balance sheets, a robust banking system, improving terms of trade (via both a higher share in global trade and a lower share of oil in GDP) and the unfolding of a structural rise in discretionary consumption.Analysts at Goldman Sachs explain their bullish stance on India. After a $64 billion peak-to-trough FII selloff, foreign ownership sits at its lowest level in more than a decade. “Since the mid-October bottom, India has received the largest share of foreign inflows within the EM pack. Valuations have de-rated significantly from peak levels, close to their 10-year average,” they say.Even as India’s earnings prospects and growth momentum are drawing foreign investors back to local stocks, there are some concerns over underlying inflation.India's retail inflation pushed past the Reserve Bank of India’s upper tolerance limit in October, with the headline rate climbing to 6.1 percent from 5.5 percent in September. This is the first breach of the 6 percent ceiling in the new Consumer Price Index (CPI) series. Food and beverages inflation accelerated to 8.5 percent from 7.4 percent. Vegetable inflation jumped to 10.9 percent, the highest in the new series, even as wholesale vegetable prices began to cool.While Goldman Sachs economists expect real GDP growth to moderate to 7.2 percent year-on-year in 2027 (from 7.9 percent year-on-year in 2026), they “expect above-consensus headline inflation of 5.7 percent YoY in 2027, amid El-Niño-related weather disruptions and high input costs, driving the view that there should be further monetary tightening ahead.”Desai and Parekh of Morgan Stanley also agree that, from a policy perspective, there is hardly anything wrong with the Indian economy except for some upside risk to inflation. “While we see far-reaching reforms that could lift growth rates in the coming quarters, policymakers could also roll out policies to directly alleviate the pain in equities,” they explain.

stories.headline: US proposes 25 per cent tariffs on India; 17 per cent if trade deal clinched
stories.title: US proposes 25 per cent tariffs on India; 17 per cent if trade deal clinched
stories.summary: Washington, Nov 25: The US on Wednesday proposed 25 per cent tariffs on Indian goods in the absence of a trade deal, citing excess industrial capacity, sustained market access barriers and inadequate labour protection that harm American companies. The US Trade Representative (USTR) said the tariffs on India would amount to 17 per cent if it agrees to a trade deal with America. The fresh tariff proposal follows Section 301 investigations launched by the USTR in March targeting 16 economic jurisdictions. The USTR proposed tariffs of up to 20 per cent to 35 per cent on other targeted economies, though lower rates apply to trading partners with deals in place. The EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland face 15 per cent tariff rates, inclusive of standard import duties. Vietnam would face tariffs of 20 per cent if the trade deal is finalised. “For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labour suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market-distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America's manufacturing base,” said USTR Jamieson Greer. “India generates trade surpluses in sectors such as pharmaceuticals, steel, and ICT goods, revealing dependencies on Indian manufacturing in certain key sectors,” the USTR said in its report on ‘India's Acts, Policies, and Practices Relating to Structural Excess Capacity and Production in Manufacturing Sectors’. These new tariffs would not be added to existing ones aimed at combating forced labour or certain sector-specific tariffs, a senior US official said. The USTR has decided to schedule public hearings on its proposals on January 25 and sought written comments from interested persons by January 5. The Office of the USTR has been analysing for several months whether 16 jurisdictions have policies that favour surplus production, a practice that drives down prices and harms US industry. The investigation began last March, after the Supreme Court overturned the indiscriminate trade levies imposed by the Trump administration invoking the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). After that reversal, the USTR opened two investigations based on Article 301: one directed at 60 jurisdictions (about a hundred countries) for violating export regulations on forced labour; and the other against 16 jurisdictions for promoting surplus production. India and the US are negotiating an interim bilateral trade agreement after the framework they had finalised in February went back to the discussion board with the Supreme Court striking down the IEEPA tariffs imposed last year. India is seeking lower tariffs for its goods in the US market than its competitors such as Bangladesh, Vietnam and Cambodia. “USTR is applying to India a diagnosis built for a very different economy. India consumes most of what it produces and buys more goods from the world than it sells, so it is not exporting a domestic glut,” said Abhik Sengupta, a Task Force Observer on the Committee on Strategic Trade and Market Access, Helsinki Geoeconomics Society. Sengupta said India’s reliance on Chinese inputs points to gaps in its industrial base, not a surplus. “Penalising India for closing those gaps risks pushing supply chains back toward the very economies Washington is most concerned about,” he said.

article_sentences: If shifting political allegiance under the guise of dissent is permitted then elected governments can be destabilised by engineering defections even among a handful of legislators, the Uddhav Thackeray-led faction told the Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was told by senior advocate Kapil Sibal that the Maharashtra Assembly Speaker committed a constitutional error by treating the Eknath Shinde group’s legislative majority as proof that it represented the original Shiv Sena.

Mr. Sibal, advancing rejoinder submissions on behalf of the Thackeray faction, said that the legislative majority cannot transform a legislature party into the original political party under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.
The defence of the Shinde group that it had expressed dissent was not even the foundation of the Speaker's decision recognising it as the original Shiv Sena.

"If shifting political allegiance under the guise of dissent is permitted, governments can be destabilised by engineering defections even among a handful of legislators," Mr. Sibal told the Bench which is likely to reserve the verdict on the two petitions.

The lead plea, filed by Sunil Prabhu of the Uddhav Thackeray faction, challenges the Maharashtra Assembly speaker's January 10, 2024 decision declining to disqualify the MLAs of the Shinde faction under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.
A connected plea filed by Mr. Thackeray challenges the ECI’s decision recognising the Shinde faction as the official Shiv Sena and allotting it the party symbol.
During the hearing, Mr. Sibal submitted that the Speaker's approach was contrary to the Constitution Bench ruling in the Subhash Desai case.

"The identity of the original political party has to be determined with reference to June 21, 2022, when the alleged act of defection first occurred," Mr. Sibal said, adding that the Election Commission’s subsequent recognition of a faction under the Symbols Order could not retrospectively determine whether an earlier act amounted to defection.
He also emphasised that disqualification proceedings before the Speaker and proceedings before the Election Commission were legally distinct and could not be conflated.
"This is not an act of dissent, but an attempt to topple the government", he said.

Countering the Shinde faction's argument that its legislators had merely dissented against the Thackeray leadership, Mr. Sibal said their actions went beyond an expression of disagreement and were aimed at displacing the government led by Mr. Thackeray.

stories.headline: Fresh proposal for additional border bunkers submitted to MHA: Chief Secretary
stories.title: Fresh proposal for additional border bunkers submitted to MHA: Chief Secretary
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 25: A fresh proposal for construction of additional bunkers along the Line of Control has been submitted to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and is at an advanced stage of consideration, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Secretary Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav said on Wednesday. He was addressing residents during a Block Diwas-cum-public grievances redressal camp at vibrant village Bhawani in Nowshera block of Rajouri district. Responding to the demand for additional bunkers, Yadav said, "A fresh proposal has been submitted to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs. It is at an advanced stage of consideration." As many as 2,783 underground bunkers have been built for the safety of civilians along the Line of Control (LoC) in Rajouri district. Of these, 1,528 were constructed by the Rural Development Department and the Public Works Department completed 1,255, according to official figures. The demand for additional safety bunkers has gained significance in the backdrop of intense Pakistani shelling and drone attacks on forward villages during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, in which 27 people, mostly civilians, were killed and 70 people were injured in Jammu and Kashmir. The Union Territory has a 221-kilometre-long International Border along the districts of Kathua, Samba and Jammu, while the Line of Control stretches for 744 kilometres, making civilian protection in border areas a key security and infrastructure priority. The programme provided a platform to residents and public representatives to raise developmental issues and seek timely intervention by the administration. Among the major demands raised were granting shrine status to Maa Mangla Mata Temple, organising a border tourism mela, double-laning of the Nowshera-Jhangar road, construction of additional bunkers, filling vacancies in educational institutions, setting up a sports stadium at Kalsian and providing healthcare facilities, including a dispensary and ambulance service, at Bhawani. Assuring residents that their demands would be examined by the departments concerned, Yadav directed the Rajouri deputy commissioner to prepare a comprehensive development plan for Maa Mangla Mata Shrine, keeping in view its religious significance and tourism potential. Regarding staff shortage in border schools, he said the matter would be taken up with the education department. He also directed the deputy commissioner to identify suitable land for the proposed sports stadium in Kalsian and asked officials to explore the development of indoor sports facilities in schools with higher student enrolment. Appropriate measures would be explored to provide a dispensary and ambulance services in Bhawani, Yadav said, adding that the demand for a Kendriya Vidyalaya would also be taken up. The chief secretary encouraged local youth to explore entrepreneurship, skill development and startup opportunities to contribute to the socio-economic development of border areas. He also directed officials to sensitise residents about collateral-free loans, startup financing and other government support schemes. During the programme, Yadav distributed sanction letters to beneficiaries of the Holistic Agriculture Development Programme and Sheep Husbandry schemes. He also handed over engagement orders to newly appointed Anganwadi workers.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves continuation of Estates Management Scheme for Department of Posts with an outlay of Rs 1,491 crore
stories.title: Cabinet approves continuation of Estates Management Scheme for Department of Posts with an outlay of Rs 1,491 crore
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 25: The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Department of Posts for the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme, the Estates Management Scheme, during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. The scheme carries a total financial outlay of Rs.1,491 crores over a five-year period. The scheme aims to comprehensively transform and modernize the estates infrastructure of the Department of Posts. It focuses heavily on the construction, re-construction, renovation, uniform branding of post offices and residential colonies, along with the preservation of India’s heritage postal buildings. This modernization strategy directly supports first-mile delivery, fosters financial inclusion and enhances citizen centric service delivery nationwide, aligning with the broader visions of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. As one of the world's largest postal networks with 1.65 lakh post offices (including 1,49,385 in rural areas), India Post remains a critical vehicle for mails, banking (POSB/IPPB), insurance (PLI), Aadhaar services, Post Office Passport Seva Kendras and rural artisan support via Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs). The scheme is scheduled for phased implementation over a five-year horizon, starting from FY 2026-27 through FY 2030-31. Key Components of the Approved Scheme: New Construction (Rs. 280 Crore): Building 190 departmental postal buildings on vacant departmental plots to replace currently rented spaces and eliminate rental liabilities. Re-construction (Rs. 108 Crore): Demolishing and rebuilding 50 dilapidated departmental postal structures to ensure long-term structural safety. Renovation & Branding (Rs. 318 Crore): Upgrading and establishing uniform branding across 2,550 departmental SubPost Offices as per SPA guidelines. Rented Post Office Upgrades (Rs. 37.50 Crore): Upgrading and uniformly branding 2,500 post offices operating out of rented premises. Heritage Preservation (Rs. 180 Crore): Restoring and preserving 20 landmark heritage postal buildings to safeguard the historical legacy of the department. Colony Renovation (Rs. 357.50 Crore): Revamping 150 high demand postal residential colonies to elevate employee welfare and satisfaction. Allied & Inclusive Activities (Rs. 100 Crore): Implementing sustainable features (Solar power, Rainwater Harvesting) and universal accessibility infrastructure (ramps, Braille signage) under the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, alongwith gender-focused additions like ladies toilets and feeding rooms. Integrated Technology Center (Rs. 100 Crore): Setting up a permanent physical infrastructure for the Centre for Excellence in Postal Technology (CEPT) in Bengaluru to drive Advanced Postal Technology (APT) services and support the indigenous Opensource Tech Stack.

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25) granted bail to three former senior officials of Rajasthan's Public Health Engineering Department (PHED), accused of facilitating the alleged award of tenders worth approximately ₹979.45 crore under the Jal Jeevan Mission through forged work-experience certificates.

A bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu allowed the appeals filed by former Additional Chief Secretary and PHED Finance Committee Chairman Subodh Agarwal, former Chief Engineer Dinesh Goel, and former Superintending Engineer Mahendra Prakash Soni, setting aside the Rajasthan High Court's orders rejecting their bail pleas.
The Court noted that the investigation against the appellants had concluded and chargesheets had been filed.
It also took into account that the trial was likely to be prolonged, given the voluminous documentary evidence and the proposed examination of 124 witnesses.
Charges were yet to be framed.

The bench observed that keeping the accused in further pre-trial custody would serve no useful purpose, particularly when several co-accused, including the then Rajasthan PHED Minister Mahesh Chandra Joshi, had already been granted bail.
The Court reiterated that the seriousness of the allegations in an economic offence cannot, by itself, justify prolonged incarceration of an undertrial.
“Pre-trial incarceration cannot masquerade as punitive detention.” the Court observed, referring to its earlier order granting bail to co-accused persons in the case.

It added that although the allegations of institutional collusion in a public welfare project were grave, their severity could not operate as an absolute bar to bail or justify keeping an accused in custody when there was no prospect of an early conclusion of the trial.
The case arose from allegations of large-scale irregularities in the implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission in Rajasthan.

According to the prosecution, between 2021 and 2023, two private contracting firms, M/s Shri Ganpati Tubewell Company and M/s Shri Shyam Tubewell Company, allegedly obtained forged work-experience certificates purportedly issued by IRCON International Limited.
Using these certificates, the firms allegedly secured work orders in approximately 104 tenders worth ₹979.45 crore, in connivance with senior public servants.

stories.headline: FWICE opposes release of Fawad Khan-starrer Pakistani show in India
stories.title: FWICE opposes release of Fawad Khan-starrer Pakistani show in India
stories.summary: Mumbai, Nov 25 : The Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) has objected to the proposed Indian release of the upcoming Pakistani Netflix series ‘Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo’. Ashoke Pandit, the chief advisor to the FWICE explained the reason behind objections to the release of the show in India. ‘Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo’ stars Fawad Khan, Hania Aamir, Hamza Ali Abbasi, Mahira Khan and others. The body has formally written to the Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi, requesting him to intervene and halt the release of the series, which is scheduled to drop on December 4, 2026, globally. Ashoke Pandit, the chief advisor to the FWICE, spoke with IANS, and addressed the issue, as he said that Pakistan is an enemy nation, and has consistently undertaken actions which harm the integrity of India. He told IANS, “We take strict objection to this entire screening of this show which is based in Pakistan and has Pakistani performers, in India because we very strongly feel that Pakistan is an enemy country. Actors like Hamza and Fawad. Hamza was a person who had literally abused and made a mockery of our Operation Sindoor. They have quite often made fun of our security forces, our country”. He further mentioned, “So, a country which doesn't believe in humanity, a country which doesn't believe in oneness, in togetherness, in non-violence, how can a channel which is based in our country screen a show which has come out of Pakistan. This is basically a Pakistani show? So, we at the federation level, we have appealed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji to take serious action against the telecast of this show and take a strong note about it and also the I&B Ministry, and Home Ministry to put a stop to this”. He warned of non-cooperation in case things are not heard, and the show gets a release in India. “If things are not heard, we will be forced to issue a non-cooperation order where our people, our industry people, our technicians, our workers will not be a part of any shows which have been shot here and are meant for Netflix. So, I am sure, I hope that things will be considered, things will be understood and understanding our emotions and the emotions of our country that this issue will be sorted out”, he added. Last year in May, the FWICE had issued an advisory directing OTT platforms, media streaming platforms and intermediaries operating in India to discontinue web series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming media content originating from Pakistan, keeping in view national security considerations and the prevailing circumstances. The federation has issued clear directives to all its affiliated associations, members and stakeholders of the Indian entertainment industry, instructing them to refrain from employing, engaging, collaborating or working with Pakistani artists and professionals in Indian films, television programmes, web series, music videos and other entertainment productions. The federation has also expressed its solidarity with the concerns raised by the All India Cine Workers Association (AICWA), which approached the Prime Minister on November 24, 2026, seeking a ban on the Indian release of the said Pakistani series. Apart from this, another Pakistani show ‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ starring Sheheryar Munawar received backlash in India after its watch party was organised in Delhi. The Pakistani romantic drama has found sizable fan-following in India. After the social media backlash, the organisers cancelled the show’s watch party in Bengaluru. ( IANS) aa/

stories.headline: IPL 2027 auction sees 1,220 registrations from Indian, foreign players
stories.title: IPL 2027 auction sees 1,220 registrations from Indian, foreign players
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 25 : A whopping 1,220 players have been named in the IPL 2027 Auction Register, the tournament's statement said on Wednesday. The list includes 939 Indians and 281 overseas players, but only 66 of them can secure contracts when franchises bid in the auction to be held in Goa on December 16. The ten franchises have already retained 184 players ahead of the auction, and no more than 25 of the open slots can go to overseas cricketers. The register is heavily tilted towards uncapped talent, with 994 players who have not played international cricket registering for it. The rest are 184 capped players and 42 cricketers from Associate nations. The list is divided into six categories. Capped internationals are at 170, and capped Indians are at 14. The other four are the 42 Associate players, the 127 uncapped Indians with IPL experience, the 798 uncapped Indians who have never featured in the league before and the 69 uncapped overseas players. Australia has the most overseas players on the register, with 53 representatives. South Africa have 40, while West Indies 36, New Zealand 25, Afghanistan 23 and Sri Lanka 21 players respectively. article_sentences: The South Peninsula remains in the grip of rain-bearing easterly disturbances, with isolated heavy rainfall likely over Kerala and Mahe, and Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, for two days from Thursday.

Strong surface winds are also expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam, and Rayalaseema, as a combination of easterly waves, atmospheric troughs and cyclonic circulations sustains unsettled weather across the region.
The wave is a westward-moving disturbance embedded in the easterly winds over the Bay of Bengal.

As it travels towards Sri Lanka and the Tamil Nadu coast, it carries enhanced cyclonic vorticity and a zone of atmospheric convergence, or conditions that encourage air to rise, cool and condense into rain-bearing clouds.
Its passage can also reinforce existing troughs and strengthen wind convergence, cloud development and rainfall.
Showers generally occur along and behind the wave trough, while sinking air ahead of it tends to favour relatively fairer or drier weather.

On Wednesday afternoon existing upper cyclonic circulations over and around the South Peninsula had weakened, though a productive trough held its end up connecting Gulf of Mannar to south-west Bay of Bengal off Tamil Nadu coast.
The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) total column water (TCW) analysis offers another indication of the moisture-rich atmosphere.

The field, which measures the total water vapour contained in a vertical column extending from the surface to the top of the atmosphere, shows values of around 100 kg per square metre (kg/m²) along a belt covering south Coastal Andhra Pradesh, north Tamil Nadu and Chennai, and the south Tamil Nadu coast.
Forecast until Thursday mid-morning, this belt extend to Tirunelveli-Nagercoil.
A TCW value of 100 kg/m² is equivalent to a theoretical rainfall depth of 10 cm if all the moisture in that atmospheric column were to condense and reach the ground.
This, however, is not a rainfall forecast.
